userStories.title: Run setup stops migrating
acceptanceCriteria: setupRun with a valid PRD, in a temp project whose `.nax/config.json` sets `outputDir` equal to the mocked `runtime.outputDir` and whose `.nax/` holds `features/demo/sessions/s1.json`, `features/demo/status.json` and `features/demo/stories/US-001/context-manifest-a.json`, leaves all three files at their original paths with their original contents.

After that setupRun call, with the mocked `runtime.outputDir` set to a directory inside the temp dir, `<runtime.outputDir>/features/demo/` holds no `sessions` entry, no `status.json` and no `stories` entry; its only entry is the `nax.lock` that `acquireFeatureLock` writes.

That setupRun call, with log entries captured through a copy of the local `captureLogs` helper from the tracked-candidates integration test, records no entry whose message starts with `Auto-migration` or with `Found generated content`.

After releasing both locks the first call took (`releaseLock(workdir)` and the feature lock release), a second setupRun on the same temp project records no `warn` entry whose message or `error` data contains `Migration conflict`.

routing.reasoning: Removes one seam member and one call in a single source file; run behaviour changes (no migration), so tests are required. Needs a new test with mocked runtime and temp project.

suggestedCriteria: setupRun with a valid PRD in a repo holding `.nax/metrics.json` leaves `.nax/metrics.json` in place and logs no migration line.

modifiedFiles.reason: remove the `autoMigrateGeneratedContent` member of `_runSetupDeps` and its call in `setupRun`. Nothing replaces them: `setupRun` goes straight from priming the status writer to claiming the project identity.

delete the file. It pins that `setupRun` calls `_runSetupDeps.autoMigrateGeneratedContent` exactly once, and that is the call this story removes. The replacing invariant, in the new run-setup-no-migration test this story creates, is that `setupRun` leaves in-repo feature artifacts in place.

userStories.title: `nax migrate` without a mode refuses
acceptanceCriteria: migrateCommand({ workdir }) with neither `reclaim` nor `merge` rejects with a NaxError whose `code` is `MIGRATE_NO_MODE`.
That rejection's message is `nax migrate needs --reclaim <name> or --merge <name>`.

That call, in a temp project whose `.nax/config.json` sets `outputDir` to `<temp dir>/out` and which holds `.nax/metrics.json`, leaves `.nax/metrics.json` in place, and `<temp dir>/out` (the configured `outputDir`) does not exist afterwards.
That call, in a temp dir with no `.nax/config.json`, rejects with `MIGRATE_NO_MODE`, not with `MIGRATE_NO_CONFIG`.
Spawning `bun bin/nax.ts migrate -d <temp project>`, with `NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR` set to a temp dir, exits with code 1.
That spawn's stderr contains `nax migrate needs --reclaim <name> or --merge <name>`.
Spawning `bun bin/nax.ts migrate --dry-run -d <temp project>`, with `NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR` set to a temp dir, exits with a non-zero code, and its stderr contains `unknown option '--dry-run'`.
Spawning `bun bin/nax.ts migrate --help`, with `NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR` set to a temp dir, prints `Recover a project-name collision: --reclaim or --merge`.

Spawning `bun bin/nax.ts migrate --reclaim <name>`, with `NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at a temp dir that holds a `<name>/` directory, exits 0 and leaves a `_archive/<name>-<timestamp>/` directory under that config dir.

routing.reasoning: Touches migrate.ts, bin/nax.ts, two existing tests, a new CLI spawn test and the complexity baseline; CLI contract changes with clear requirements and no new abstractions.

migrateCommand({ workdir, reclaim: <a>, merge: <b> }) runs the reclaim branch, as before.

analysis: Goal: remove nax's generated-content migration (the auto-migration at the start of every `nax run` and the default `nax migrate` move). `nax migrate --reclaim <name>` and `--merge <name>` stay unchanged; they recover project-name collisions. Bare `nax migrate` becomes a usage error (NaxError MIGRATE_NO_MODE), and `--dry-run` is removed. Why: the scan matches live in-repo data (.nax/features/<f>/sessions/, status.json, stories/<s>/context-manifest-*.json) that current nax writes and reads. The next run's auto-migration (setupRun -> _runSetupDeps.autoMigrateGeneratedContent) renames them into ~/.nax/<project>/features/..., conflicts with an earlier move, throws MIGRATE_CONFLICT and logs 'Auto-migration failed'. A successful move also takes live data away from in-repo readers. Key files (all under packages/nax unless noted): src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts (setupRun, _runSetupDeps; remove the autoMigrateGeneratedContent member and its call between status-writer priming and project-identity claim); src/commands/migrate.ts (MigrateOptions, migrateCommand, GENERATED_NAMES, GENERATED_FEATURE_SUBNAMES, detectGeneratedContent, partitionTrackedCandidates, autoMigrateGeneratedContent, MigrateCandidate, _gitDeps re-export; keep --reclaim and --merge branches in that order; mkdir and rename imports stay, gitWithTimeout/readdir/getSafeLogger/projectOutputDir imports go because biome rejects unused imports); src/commands/index.ts (exports); bin/nax.ts (~line 400, migrate command definition: drop --dry-run, new description 'Recover a project-name collision: --reclaim or --merge'; existing catch prints 'Error: <message>' in red and exits 1); scripts/baselines/complexity-baseline.json (records src/commands/migrate.ts at detectGeneratedContent: 54, migrateCommand: 41; the ratchet fails stale rows, so regenerate with `bun run check:complexity:update` in both US-002 and US-003); scripts/check-worktree-id-ssot.ts keeps migrate.ts in ALLOWED_FILES and needs no change. Tests: delete test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-auto-migrate.test.ts (US-001); create test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-no-migration.test.ts (US-001), copying the local captureLogs helper from test/integration/commands/migrate-tracked-candidates.test.ts because US-003 deletes that file; remove the 'migrateCommand — full migration flow' describe block and the chmod import from test/unit/commands/migrate.test.ts (US-002), and later the detectGeneratedContent block plus its import and the mkdir import (US-003); remove the 'US-003 migrateCommand' describe block from migrate-tracked-candidates.test.ts (US-002) then delete the whole file (US-003); create test/unit/cli/migrate-cli.test.ts (US-002), which spawns `bun bin/nax.ts` with NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR set to a temp dir (deliberate exception to the forbidden-patterns-tests rule; precedent test/unit/cli/trust.test.ts; bin/nax.ts defines the command inline and cannot be imported). Docs (US-003): docs/guides/cli-reference.md nax migrate section (drop the --dry-run example and flag-table row, describe collision recovery only, keep --reclaim/--merge examples), packages/nax/README.md migrate table row ('Recover a project-name collision: `--reclaim <name>` or `--merge <name>`'), docs/architecture/subsystems.md ~line 1745 (migrateCommand handles --reclaim/--merge project-identity collision recovery only). No source file outside migrate.ts and commands/index.ts imports the removed symbols, so the compiler is the dependency check. Risks: leaving a stale complexity baseline row fails check:all; leaving an unused import fails lint:biome; the MIGRATE_NO_MODE throw must happen before any file access (no config read, no mkdir) so that a missing .nax/config.json still yields MIGRATE_NO_MODE and a configured outputDir is never created. In US-001 tests, mock runtime.outputDir to a dir inside the temp dir and release both locks (releaseLock(workdir) and the feature lock) before a second setupRun. Never run bare `bun test` and never `bun run nax`; run package commands from packages/nax. The tracked .nax/features/run-hygiene-bugs/.nax-acceptance.test.ts imports removed functions but is out of scope (.nax/ is read-only to the run).
outOfScope: Changing `--reclaim` or `--merge` behaviour, including which of the two runs when both are passed (`--reclaim` today).
Cleaning up `~/.nax/<project>/features/*/sessions/` directories an earlier auto-migration left behind; they are harmless.
Moving any in-repo `.nax/features/<f>/` content anywhere; it stays where nax reads it.

The tracked `.nax/features/run-hygiene-bugs/.nax-acceptance.test.ts`, which imports the removed functions. `.nax/` is read-only to the run, and no package test suite, typecheck or lint covers that file. Deleting it is a manual follow-up.
Rewriting historical design documents under `docs/specs/` that describe the migration.
